content.text:
The pattern fits a single phase, Mn2CrO4 (mp-34139). I compared it by eye with simulated patterns for three of the nine candidates and did not calculate a fit score.

- **Mn2CrO4 (mp-34139):** its simulated pattern matches the observed peak groups in both position and relative height:

| Region | Observed (two-theta, intensity) | Simulated Mn2CrO4 |
|---|---|---|
| ~30° | 29.6 (47), 30.4 (21), 31.0 (28) | 29.6 (59), 30.4 (20), 30.85 (38) |
| ~35° | 34.4 (100), 35.1 (55) | 34.6 (85), 35.3 (60) |
| 36–39° | 36.2 (85), 37.0 (44), 37.9 (46), 38.6 (20), 39.3 (~13) | 36.3 (100), 37.1 (55), 37.6 (68), 38.3 (18), 39.0 (12) |

- **Other peaks:** the observed peaks near 43.7°, 53–58°, 62.8° and 66.4° also fall where the simulated pattern has peaks.
- **Low-angle peak:** this is the weakest point of the match. The observed peak sits near 17.5°, a little below the simulated one at about 18°. I did not count the grid points exactly here.
- **Two other candidates checked:** SrCa(CuO2)2 (mp-1218363) and Sr2CoSbO6 (mp-1218837) do not reproduce the observed groups of peaks.
- **Not checked:** I did not simulate the other five candidates. I also did not test whether a second phase explains the observed peak near 41.3° (intensity about 26), so a minor second phase is not ruled out.

{"present": ["mp-34139"], "confidence": 0.8, "note": "The main peak groups near 30, 35, 37, 44, 56, 63 and 66 degrees match the simulated Mn2CrO4 pattern; two other candidates were checked and rejected, five were not simulated, and a minor second phase was not ruled out."}
